subject: Architecture
title: Mass Timber: Wood Challenges Concrete
description: A short lesson to help you apply Mass Timber: Wood Challenges Concrete.

hook.text: Eighteen-story buildings are now being built from wood. Not log cabins — engineered timber towers.

buildup.text: Cross-laminated timber (CLT) is glued in alternating layers, creating panels as strong as steel.

discovery.text: Wood stores carbon. A mass timber building can be carbon-negative — absorbing more CO₂ than it emits.

twist.text: Thick timber chars on the surface during fire but doesn't collapse — steel melts at lower temperatures.

climax.text: Mjøstårnet in Norway stands 18 stories tall — the world's tallest timber building.

punchline.text: Concrete ruled for a century. Trees are making a comeback.

quiz.question: How does thick timber perform in a fire compared to steel?
options: It burns faster and collapses immediately
It chars on the surface but doesn't collapse; steel can melt at lower temperatures
It performs exactly the same as steel

details.summary: Mass timber construction uses engineered wood products like cross-laminated timber (CLT) to build structures up to 25 stories tall. Lighter, faster to assemble, and dramatically lower in carbon emissions than steel or concrete, mass timber is reshaping how architects think about tall buildings.
details.whyItMatters: Concrete production generates 8% of global CO₂ emissions. Mass timber sequesters carbon instead of emitting it, offering a structural alternative that could fundamentally reduce construction's climate impact while creating beautiful warm interiors.
takeaways: Mass timber uses engineered wood like CLT for large-scale construction
Buildings up to 25 stories have been built with mass timber
It sequesters carbon rather than emitting it like concrete

faq.question: Is mass timber safe in fires?
faq.answer: Counterintuitively, large timber members perform well in fire. They form a protective char layer that insulates the inner wood, maintaining structural integrity longer than unprotected steel, which softens at high temperatures. Building codes increasingly recognize mass timber's fire performance.

faq.question: Where are the tallest mass timber buildings?
faq.answer: Mjøstårnet in Norway (85.4 meters, 18 stories) and Ascent in Milwaukee, USA (86.6 meters, 25 stories) are among the tallest. Projects under development aim higher. Each new record demonstrates that timber can compete with steel and concrete at scale.
